economic_intuition.value: Growing evidence identifies a bias in the market's capitalization of corporate asset investment and disinvestment: events associated with asset expansion tend to be followed by abnormally low returns, and events associated with asset contraction tend to be followed by abnormally high returns, consistent with investors overextrapolating past growth.

notes: Manually re-derived MethodSpec, independently constructed directly from the paper PDF (Cooper, Gulen, and Schill (2008), JF 63(4):1609-1651) as a ground-truth reference, without consulting any prior extraction. Primary sort is the single-dimension annual asset-growth decile sort (Table I/II); VW portfolios and FF3 alphas selected as primary results since the paper leads with VW spreads in the abstract (8% per year) and Table II Panel C.2 reports the 'All Firms' VW FF3 alpha spread. EW portfolios and raw-return spreads are also reported by the paper but not captured here as separate metrics (max_length=4 cap; EW spread is the larger, ~20%/year effect -- see Table II Panel C.1). The paper does not state whether decile breakpoints for the main asset-growth sort are computed on the full sample or NYSE-only (NYSE breakpoints are explicitly used only for a separate market-cap decile comparison in footnote 7); breakpoints.basis is therefore marked unspecified/inferred as full_sample. Winsorizing the asset-growth distribution at the 1st/99th percentiles is described only as a robustness check (Section II.B, p.1632), not part of the baseline construction, so no TransformSpec is included. The 2-year Compustat listing-duration backfill-bias screen has no registered physical column in this engine's data layer and is recorded as accepted_unapplied.
